statements.context: f WASHINGTON October 21, 2026 – Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Christopher J. Mahoney delivered a keynote address to mid-career and senior military officers at the National Defense University (NDU) on Oct. 20, outlining a comprehensive framework for strategic leadership in an era of rapid technological and geopolitical change. NDU serves as the premier institution for joint professional military education under the direction of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Speaking as part of the National War College’s prestigious Kennan Lecture Series, Gen. Mahoney addressed an audience of select O-5 and O-6 officers preparing for high-level joint command assignments, including command. Drawing on paired strategists from Sun Tzu and Clausewitz to George C. Marshall, Gen. Mahoney offered four insights for leaders moving into senior strategic roles: speed is nothing without judgment; leaders must understand the nature of the fight they have, not the fight they want; the trust of the Nation is a strategic advantage; and candor is a duty, while execution is an obligation. Speed Without Judgment Is a Trap While acknowledging that advanced sensors and super intelligence offer unprecedented capabilities from "cislunar to the seabed," Gen. Mahoney warned that rapid data processing does not equate to genuine situational understanding. He invoked Air Force strategist Colonel John Boyd’s thinking to highlight the danger of bad information being rapidly validated by automated systems. "Speed does not connote understanding,” said Gen. Mahoney. “Do not ever outsource your judgment... Because if you’re making the wrong decisions, you’re just losing faster."
